transcript: I want to talk about the contemporary musical theater style of music. You know it, you've heard it, you've seen it mocked on TikTok. It feels like something out of the past, and what business does it have continuing to exist? But then sometimes I see these shows, and when I'm actually sitting in the theater, I find that it usually doesn't bother me that much. This has been on my mind because of two shows I saw in the last couple weeks, how to dance in Ohio and walk on through, both of which I thought had problems, but I didn't really mind that they employed this style of music. I will say I think the score of walk On Through was at its best when he was letting other genre influences bleed in. So in that sense, I guess I did gravitate away from that more generic Sound. With walk on through, he was still able to experiment with form and use the music to create compelling links between his life and the paintings, and just in general use it to be vulnerable and express his deepest fears and insecurities. When it comes to how to dance in Ohio, I thought, I don't know, that there was an outside genre that was intuitively screaming to be utilized to tell this story. So I guess the takeaway here is that while I'm probably still never gonna be drawn to this style, I'm probably never gonna listen to these cast albums, and it's still probably not what I want personally for the future of musical theater.
